title: React Architecture & Next.js
tagline: Component reconciliation, hook lifecycles, Server Components, and production state patterns
description: Deep dive into React 19, Fiber reconciler internals, concurrent rendering, custom hooks, Server Components (RSC), and production Next.js App Router patterns.

stages.title: Stage 1: Core React & Reconciliation
stages.description: JSX, Virtual DOM, Fiber tree architecture, and render vs commit phases.

nodes.title: React Fiber Architecture & Re-rendering Rules
nodes.description: How React divides work into incremental units (Fibers), performs reconciliation with diffing algorithms, and batches state updates.
nodes.whyItMatters: Unnecessary re-renders in large component trees slow down user interactions. Knowing what causes a render allows surgical optimization.
keyTakeaways: A component re-renders when its state changes or its parent re-renders (unless memoized).
Never use array indices as keys if items can be reordered, inserted, or deleted.
React 18+ automatically batches multiple state updates even inside async callbacks.
nodes.interviewTips: Explain why React moved from the legacy stack reconciler to the Fiber reconciler, and what priority-based interruptible rendering means.

stages.title: Stage 2: Hooks Deep-Dive & Performance
stages.description: useState, useEffect, useMemo, useCallback, useTransition, and custom hook encapsulation.

nodes.title: Advanced Hooks & Concurrent Features
nodes.description: Managing side effects safely, avoiding stale closures, and using useTransition to mark non-urgent state updates for instant UI responsiveness.
nodes.whyItMatters: Improper useEffect dependency arrays create infinite render loops or subtle stale closure bugs. useTransition keeps typing inputs snappy during heavy list filtering.

resources.title: React Docs: You Might Not Need an Effect
Overreacted: A Complete Guide to useEffect

keyTakeaways: Do not use useEffect for calculating derived state; compute it during render.
useCallback and useMemo only help if passing callbacks to memoized children or computing heavy math.
useTransition lets React yield to user interactions while rendering expensive views.
nodes.interviewTips: Expect scenario questions where a useEffect captures a stale state variable, and you must resolve it with functional state updater or useRef.

stages.title: Stage 3: Server Components & Next.js
stages.description: React Server Components (RSC), streaming HTML with Suspense, Server Actions, and Next.js App Router.

nodes.title: React Server Components (RSC) & Streaming
nodes.description: Executing components exclusively on the server to eliminate zero-bundle-size client overhead, access databases directly, and stream UI with Suspense.
nodes.whyItMatters: Traditional client bundles send megabytes of JS to the browser. RSC keeps dependencies on the server, drastically accelerating Time to Interactive.

resources.title: Dan Abramov: React Server Components Mental Model

keyTakeaways: Server Components do not ship JavaScript to the client; Client Components require 'use client' at the top.
Pass Server Components as children to Client Components to avoid forcing the whole subtree into the client bundle.
Use React Suspense to stream slow database queries into the browser without blocking the initial page layout.
nodes.interviewTips: Be prepared to explain the architectural boundaries between 'use client' and 'use server' directives in modern Next.js.
